subject.title: [Feature/RFC]: Add eval-backed option discovery to avoid premature convergence in route/strategy answers

question: Should OpenClaw make eval-backed option discovery / anti-premature-convergence a default behavior invariant for route, strategy, and choice answers, or keep it as an opt-in research/profile behavior?
rationale: The current code can support adjacent tool use and web search, but the requested invariant changes default answer strategy, runtime prompt scope, and cost/latency expectations, so automation should not choose it as a bug fix.

options.title: Adopt eval-first default invariant
options.body: Authorize a generic QA Lab scenario first, then implement the narrow shared behavior contract only after the eval shape and runtime-pair scope are accepted.

options.title: Keep it opt-in
options.body: Route the behavior to a research or best-insight profile so default OpenClaw remains lean and lower-latency.

options.title: Decline the invariant
options.body: Close the issue with a product decision that locally defensible recommendations are acceptable unless the user explicitly asks for broader exploration.

recommendation.title: Adopt eval-first default invariant
recommendation.body: Authorize a generic QA Lab scenario first, then implement the narrow shared behavior contract only after the eval shape and runtime-pair scope are accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and adjacent Codex/web-search work make this the strongest available routing candidate for the product/runtime decision.
